# Gazetteer Overview and Methodology (10000BC - 1300AD)

This companion document details the settlement-level gazetteer (`galicia_and_volhynia_settlements.json`, comprising 185 distinct archaeological sites and pre-Mongol and devolved-principality settlements) for Region 3 (Galicia and Volhynia) of the Kievan Rus regional sub-series (10000BC - 1300AD). All benchmark series are strictly book-ended at the Mongol Conquests (1240-1241AD campaign of Batu Khan across Volhynia and Galicia) and the immediate post-conquest Romanovichi Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia (Kingdom of Rus) (1250AD - 1300AD) [@krypyakevych1984galicia; @kotlyar1998galician; @vojtovych2011borders].

## Archaeological Planimetry and Density Multipliers

Population estimates for individual settlements in `galicia_and_volhynia_settlements.json` are derived from three primary archaeological and chronicle methodologies:

1. **Prehistoric, Eneolithic and Early Iron Age Planimetry** (10000BC - 300AD):
 - ***Upper Palaeolithic and Neolithic** (10000BC - 5000BC)*: Derived from multilayered Dniester canyon and Tisza periglacial camp horizons at Molodova I and V, Korman IV, Babin I, Voronovitsa, Korolevo and Kulychivka (110 - 220 inhabitants) and Bug-Dniester and Linear Pottery (*LBK*) agricultural villages at Soroky, Bazkiv Ostriv and Nezvysko (280 - 420 inhabitants) [@chernysh1987molodova; @videiko2004trypillia].
 - ***Trypillia-Cucuteni Dniester-Prut-Bug Centres** (3500BC)*: Derived from promontory and concentric settlements across the Upper and Middle Dniester, Horyn flint-mining zone and Southern Bug (Stina 3 000, Bilche-Zolote (Verteba Cave) 2 500, Koshylivtsi 2 500, Zalishchyky 2 200, Nemyriv 2 200, Bodaki 2 000, Klishchiv 2 000, Horodnytsia 1 800, Shypyntsi 1 800) [@videiko2004trypillia].
 - ***Scythian West Podolian Giant Hillforts and Chernyakhov Centres** (500BC - 300AD)*: Derived from the 110 ha earthen rampart enclosure at Nemyriv (4 500), Severynivka (2 500) and Hryhorivka (2 200) and from the Roman-era Chernyakhov, Lipitsa and Wielbark craft centres at Lepesivka (1 500), Ripniv II (1 400), Bovshiv (1 200) and Cherneliv-Ruskyi (1 100) [@smirnova1990nemyriv; @magomedov2001chernyakhov].
2. **Galician-Volhynian Fortified Enclosures** (Gorodishcha) and Suburbs (Posady, 800AD - 1240AD):
 - Following the urban archaeological syntheses of P. P. Tolochko [@tolochko1989goroda; @tolochko2001demography], A. V. Kuza [@kuza1989malye; @kuza1996gorodishcha], V. M. Petehyrych [@petehyrych2006galicia], B. P. Tomenchuk [@tomenchuk2006halych] and S. V. Tersky [@tersky2006lutsk], fortified towns are partitioned into the inner princely citadel (*detinets*), outer rampart enclosure (*okolnyi grad*) and unfortified artisan quarters (*posady* and *pidhoroddia*).
 - Compact multi-rampart capitals such as Volodymyr (75 ha, 22 000), Zvenyhorod (45 ha, 10 000), Lutsk (40 ha, 10 000), Peremyshl (38 ha, 9 000), Kholm (36 ha, 8 000 in 1240AD), Terebovlia (30 ha, 6 500), Belz (28 ha, 6 000), Bakota (26 ha, 5 500), Peresopnytsia (24 ha, 5 000), Dorogobuzh-on-Horyn (22 ha, 4 500), Kamianets (22 ha, 4 000) and Kremenets (20 ha, 4 000) reflect mean urban densities of 200 - 290 persons/ha across combined *detinets* and core *posad* areas. Conversely, polycentric complexes enclosing meadows, monasteries and river ports - notably Halych (*Krylos*) (200 ha, 30 000, 150 persons/ha), Vasyliv (35 ha, 5 000, 143 persons/ha) and the early tribal enclosures of Plisnesk (160 ha) and Stilsko (200 ha) - reflect lower overall enclosure densities [@fylypchuk2012plisnesk; @tomenchuk2006halych].
3. **Mongol Conquest Destruction Horizons and Kingdom of Rus Restructuring** (1240AD - 1300AD):
 - Calibrated to the 1240-1241AD archaeological destruction layers excavated at Iziaslavl (2 800 in 1200AD to 600 in 1250AD) [@karger1964iziaslavl], Kolodyazhyn (2 200 to 450), Zvenyhorod (10 000 to 2 500), Halych (30 000 to 10 000) and Volodymyr (22 000 to 12 000), contrasted against the unconquered cliff citadels of Kremenets (4 000 in 1200AD to 4 500 in 1250AD and 5 500 in 1300AD) and Danyliv and King Daniel and Lev Danilovich's new royal capitals at Kholm (12 000 in 1300AD) and Lviv (12 000 in 1300AD) [@kotlyar2002chronicle; @rappoport1967military].
